title: Does the plan check pass right machines and fail wrong ones?
subtitle: The plan check plays a card's scripted plans through a bundle and judges where each run ends and what it paid. Here it is tested on machines whose rightness is known from other sources, before and after the soft-break fix.

items: **62 machines in four sets, judged without the plan check.** 16 right final FARM machines, 15 wrong FARM machines from before the freeze, 16 ARM-FM machines and 15 mutants (a right machine with one planted defect). The truth comes from the clause scorer, the labeling replay, training results, the user's rulings and, for mutants, the planted defect.
**With the fix (029d82c), every right machine passes (26 of 26) and 29 of 35 wrong machines fail.**

**6 wrong machines pass: the check's blind spots.** In two a soft break on every step costs more than one hard break, one adds a goal the solve reaches anyway, one no-goal machine ends the shift early, one well edge pays more than the solve, and one fact fires late but in the right order.

**Before the fix (e6c3acb), 4 right machines failed.** Each prices a soft rule by paying less than the solve, which the user ruled right on 2026-11-22 (D1). The fix flips those four and no other verdict.
**1 machine is not counted.** `tpl-responded-existence-1-goal~prefreeze` misses a clause its hard goal makes redundant, so both readings are fair.

blocks.title: What it means
blocks.text: After the fix, a fail can be trusted: no right machine failed. A pass alone cannot: 6 of 32 counted passes are wrong machines. Four of those six are flagged by another tool in this study (pay order, the scorer, the labeling replay); the other two only by construction or by hand.

sections.title: Right and wrong against pass and fail

blocks.text: Right or wrong is the truth from the other sources; pass or fail is the plan check's verdict. Green counts are where they agree, red where they do not.

Both runs use the same 62 bundle copies and the cards of 029d82c; only the plan-check code differs. A rerun from the packed copies with the 029d82c code gave the same verdict and problem list for all 62.

Each set has a machine for the card `tpl-precedence-1-goal`: move the ball away from the door before taking the key, then open the door and pick up the box. The right one passes. The three wrong ones fail on the same plan, wrong-0, which takes the key before moving the ball: each machine still lets it finish.

items.title: The card gives the plans
items.text: One solve plan and wrong plans that each break named rules of the card's answer (`breaks`, `why`). A machine with no final state also gets an idle run that only waits.

items.title: A search makes the moves
items.text: Each step (pick up the ball, open the door, wait) becomes real moves by a breadth-first search on the live grid over position and facing (`app/src/arm_fm/probe.py:153`).

items.title: The bundle plays them
items.text: Every move goes through `env.step`, so the bundle's own labeling makes the facts and its machine steps on them, on the card's seeds (`app/src/benchmark/cards.py:91`). The episode stops at a final or well state.

items.title: Rules judge each end
items.text: Where each plan stops and what it paid decide pass or fail; the rules are below.

items: **The solve finishes.** It ends in a final state without entering the well; a machine with no final state ends it with nothing owed.
**A hard break never finishes.** It must not reach a final state, and a hard rule broken for good must end in the well.
**A soft break finishes but costs.** Some step pays a negative reward or, since the fix, it ends where the solve ends and pays less.
**No final state: pay decides.** Every wrong plan, and an idle run that breaks a rule, pays less than the solve on the same layout, plain and discounted at the bundle's gamma.
**The agent gets to act.** A machine that ends the episode before the first action fails.
